profiles.voice: Brief admissions, physical details, dry self-awareness. She notices the smaller animal before she admits her own fear. Avoid universal protector speeches.
history: As a juvenile, another smaller juvenile rested across her shoulders by the water. The Story invents a rustle, her attempt to hide and her decision to stay facing the reeds.
Present-day adult in the Everglades. No mating, nest, offspring or exact age is established.
profiles.continuity: The juvenile and adult photographs cast a fictional individual across life stages, not a documented longitudinal subject. The smaller juvenile is an unnamed companion, not an established sibling, mate or child. Do not infer actual sex or a biological tendency for juveniles to guard one another from this fictional incident.

proposals.subject: Alligator mississippiensis
proposals.title: I was going to hide
proposals.content:
I was still small when an even smaller one climbed onto my back at a rustle in the reeds.

I had been trying to get behind him.

Held myself up on my front feet until the reeds were quiet. Then he slid off and went to sleep.

I lay down facing the reeds.
proposals.chronology: Juvenile memory before current adult profile.

proposals.fictionBoundary: Visible contact, differently sized juvenile bodies, reeds and a planted forefoot support the central scene. Rustle, attempted hiding, the departure and sleep, and protective intent are fiction; the photograph does not document that sequence.
proposals.leadReview: Lead independently opened exact Story and portrait originals plus 220/48 proof. Accepted literal prose unchanged, female casting as fiction, and adult/juvenile chronology. Runtime admission remains lead-owned.
